CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc presenting for her annual exam. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel symptoms have also resolved since prior surgical release a couple of years ago, and she has returned to work with full range of motion and no numbness or tingling in her hands. However, over the last month she has been experiencing chest pain that occurs with walking and resolves with rest. She denies experiencing it at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest, occurring approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting and states the pain is not severe enough to warrant emergency evaluation. She also reports some nasal congestion attributed to allergies related to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Endorses chest pain with exertion and nasal congestion from allergies. Denies shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, or fever and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

Not documented

Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently working

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygen saturation normal
Heart: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Carotid arteries: No bruits appreciated
Extremities: No lower extremity edema; healed surgical scar on right wrist
General: Well-appearing female

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45% (slightly reduced), mild mitral regurgitation
EKG: Stable, consistent with prior coronary artery disease history, no new changes

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post release: Resolved. Continue conservative management. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
2. Herniated disc: Currently well controlled with steroid injection. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent exertional chest pain: Continue aspirin and toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Order lipid panel. Initiate crestor 20 mg once daily.
